item.title: Mark Zuckerberg, Priscilla Chan donate $4 million to save 600-year-old Hawaii fishpond
item.description: Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan have contributed $4 million for the preservation of Alakoko Fishpond in Hawaii. This historic site, which is over 600 years old, faced potential environmental degradation and development pressure. The donation helped acquire the property for long-term stewardship by the nonprofit Mālama Hulē‘ia. Their initiative supports education about traditional Hawaiian aquaculture and native ecosystems.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: ‘Took turns shooting’: Trans NYT exec killed by in-laws amid anti-LGBTQ+ allegations
item.description: Jonathan McKinsey was shot and killed by his elderly in-laws at a sports complex in California. Police arrested the suspects, Shouyong Zhang and Shili Chen, near the crime scene shortly after the incident. McKinsey's transgender identity allegedly contributed to a family conflict and legal disputes with his wife, Candice Jang. The couple was involved in divorce proceedings and allegations of domestic violence prior to McKinsey's death.
item.dc:creator: PRISHA PATNAIK

item.title: ‘UP is my karmabhoomi’: Former IAS officer Divya Mittal announces political entry
item.description: Divya Mittal has decided to enter independent politics as she announces her political journey in Uttar Pradesh. She aims to address various issues such as infrastructure, employment, and examination paper leaks, which require public attention. Mittal expressed her concerns about unresolved public problems stemming from a lack of governmental intent. She has called for collective public participation to facilitate meaningful political change.
item.dc:creator: ARVIND CHAUHAN

item.title: Neeru Dhanda scripts history with India’s first individual gold in Asian Games 2026
item.description: Neeru Dhanda celebrated a remarkable success in the women's trap individual event at the Asian Games, capturing the coveted gold medal. With a stellar start, she flawlessly hit all five of her opening shots and maintained her composure throughout the final round. Earlier in the competition, she played a pivotal role in helping the women's trap team clinch a silver medal.
item.dc:creator: PRANAV SHUKLA

item.title: Infosys to shift a third of 320,000 staff into specialist roles; here’s why
item.description: Infosys has more than 320,000 employees, but the growing impact of AI on billing models based on the number of people deployed on projects is putting pressure on the traditional headcount-driven pricing structure. The Bengaluru-headquartered IT services company is recruiting talent from leading Indian institutes as well as US campuses, with the company often competing with AI labs for the same pool of candidates.

item.title: 2,400-year-old school where Aristotle taught Alexander unearthed in Greece
item.description: In an extraordinary archaeological discovery in northern Greece, a gymnasium complex tied to Alexander the Great's education has emerged in Mieza. Believed to have been established by King Philip II, this site functioned as a prestigious institution for the elite. Recent excavations revealed various structures, including banquet halls used for social gatherings and teaching facilities, hinting at Aristotle's influence on students like Alexander.
item.dc:creator: TOI SCIENCE DESK

item.title: Illinois man’s 100-acre conservation work helps protect water for 30,000 people
item.description: Greg Reising began his conservation work on his 100-acre property near Kinkaid Lake in 1995. He transformed former agricultural land by establishing prairie vegetation and planting thousands of trees. Erosion and sedimentation problems in the Kinkaid Lake watershed led to broader conservation efforts involving various agencies. The Environmental Quality Incentives Program supported Reising's initiatives, including streambank stabilization and habitat improvement measures.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Anthropic flags billions in losses and AI risks ahead of IPO as Dario Amodei urges caution
item.description: Anthropic's IPO prospectus reveals a net loss of $42 billion in 2025, highlighting the high costs of AI scaling. The company reported a 12-fold revenue increase to nearly $4.6 billion, despite operating losses exceeding $8 billion. CEO Dario Amodei emphasizes the need for caution in AI deployment while addressing competitive pressures. Anthropic aims for a valuation exceeding $2 trillion in its upcoming public offering.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Shubhanshu Shukla shows how he prepares his favourite mango salad in space
item.description: Shubhanshu Shukla shared a video showcasing the preparation of mango salad during his Axiom-4 mission. He explained that food in space requires different preparation methods based on its form. Shukla demonstrated the rehydration process by using a machine to add cold water to the dehydrated salad. He noted the absence of microwaves on the International Space Station while emphasizing the importance of preventing crumbs from floating.

item.title: Jason and Kylie Kelce’s $2.9B investment: How did it reach 5,000 stores?
item.description: Jason Kelce has made a savvy equity investment in Hank Sauce via Winnie Capital, marking a significant step for both him and the brand. Once a local staple, Hank Sauce now boasts distribution in over 5,000 stores across the country. With a U.S. hot sauce market worth nearly $2.9 billion, this partnership looks to amplify Hank Sauce's visibility and reach nationally, taking advantage of the substantial growth opportunities ahead.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Travis Kelce’s $12.35M real estate empire: How did he build it?
item.description: Travis Kelce has built an impressive real estate portfolio spanning Kansas and Ohio. His reported properties include a 17,000-square-foot Leawood mansion, a 21,000-square-foot lakefront estate in Bratenahl and a former 10,000-square-foot Kansas City home. Together, the three properties cover nearly 48,000 square feet, with reported purchase prices totalling about $12.35 million. His Leawood home also reportedly served as the setting for his 2025 proposal to Taylor Swift.

item.title: Delhi-NCR children with asthma, allergies at risk as weather patterns change
item.description: Recent shifts in Delhi-NCR's weather patterns are leading to a rise in respiratory ailments among children. Experts report an uptick in asthma, allergic rhinitis, and persistent cough, attributed to various environmental factors. It is essential for parents to identify troubling symptoms and consult healthcare professionals. Minimizing children's exposure to known irritants can significantly alleviate their symptoms, ensuring they maintain an active lifestyle.

item.title: Ordered phone, received soap instead, customer wins Rs 20,574 against Flipkart
item.description: A customer ordered a mobile phone from Flipkart but received bars of soap instead. Despite multiple complaints and a video proof, Flipkart did not resolve the issue satisfactorily. The Delhi consumer commission found Flipkart guilty of deficiency in service and unfair trade practice. Flipkart was directed to pay the customer Rs 10,574 along with compensation for mental harassment and litigation expenses.
item.dc:creator: SAURABH THAKUR

item.title: 'If EC guided by private party, then what remains?' Calcutta HC
item.description: Calcutta high court scrutinized the Election Commission's handling of symbol allocation amid a political dispute. Justice Krishna Rao indicated possible collusion between the Commission and Democratic Trinamool Congress regarding the symbol. The Indian Secular Front challenged the Commission's decision regarding the symbol ‘envelope’. ISF's counsel contended that the allocation process was both unreasonable and illegal. The court has reserved its judgment on this noteworthy case.
item.dc:creator: SUBRATA CHATTORAJ AND SRISHTI LAKHOTIA

item.title: Marching through the storm: ‘Hum Auratein Aazad Hain’ echoes across Delhi University
item.description: Women from various Delhi University colleges demonstrated for their freedom and safety against violence on Monday. They marched under the banner 'Hum Auratein Aazad Hain' despite rain, emphasizing the need for social change. Participants expressed solidarity and rejected restrictions on women's movement in response to sexual violence. The crowd included supportive men, stressing the need for changing men's attitudes toward women's safety.

item.title: Russia warns Nato of 'direct confrontation' if Kaliningrad is cut off from Russia
item.description: "Amid the aggressive policy pursued by Nato leadership and member countries, the embassy has conveyed our principled approaches to the Nato International Secretariat and the Belgian foreign minisry," TASS reported citing a statement by the Russian Embassy to Belgium, which is in charge of diplomatic contacts with the North Atlantic alliance. Kaliningrad is a Russian territory on the Baltic Sea that is separated from mainland Russia by other countries.

item.title: Khalistan groups turn to jail networks to recruit operatives across north India: Intel
item.description: Intelligence agencies are investigating pro-Khalistan groups recruiting within jails across north India. A recently detained operative disclosed connections to key figures while serving in Patiala jail. Agency investigations now focus on dead-drop recruitment methods and funding channels used by these groups. An SFJ-backed operatives was arrested after graffiti incidents linked to Khalistan activities. The arrested operative revealed a prior history of pro-Khalistan involvement and further recruitment efforts.

item.title: Delhi Police file non-cognisable report against Parvesh Verma after complaint over slap
item.description: Delhi Police has submitted a non-cognisable report after a complaint involving PWD minister Parvesh Verma. The complaint was filed by Sahib Singh, who reported being slapped by the minister. Additionally, an FIR related to extortion was registered by an assistant engineer of the PWD. AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal has demanded Verma's dismissal and arrest. Kejriwal criticized the quality of the road built in Tilak Nagar, asserting it was substandard.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: US military to guard midterms after Trump gutted agency that protects elections
item.description: The National Security Agency and other military cyber units have long assisted with monitoring election infrastructure and defending it against possible hacking attempts. Election systems were designated as “critical infrastructure” in 2017, paving the way for greater federal cybersecurity support. Hegseth's announcement comes weeks before Election Day on November 3, with early voting already underway.
